messages.content: How do I structure a deps.edn file for a Clojure project?
What are the different ways to add dependencies in deps.edn?

deps.edn supports multiple dependency sources:

**1. Maven/Clojars (Most Common)**
```clojure
{:deps {;; Standard Maven coordinate
        org.clojure/clojure {:mvn/version "1.11.1"}
        
        ;; From specific repository
        com.company/private {:mvn/version "1.0.0"
                             :mvn/repos {"private" {:url "https://repo.company.com"}}}}}
```

**2. Git Dependencies**
```clojure
{:deps {;; By SHA (most stable)
        io.github.user/repo {:git/sha "abc123def456"}
        
        ;; By tag + SHA (readable)
        io.github.user/repo {:git/tag "v1.2.3" :git/sha "abc123d"}
        
        ;; Private repo with auth
        io.github.company/private {:git/url "git@github.com:company/private.git"
                                   :git/sha "abc123"}
        
        ;; Subdirectory of monorepo
        io.github.user/monorepo {:git/sha "abc123"
                                  :deps/root "libs/subproject"}}}
```

**3. Local Dependencies**
```clojure
{:deps {;; Local JAR file
        my/lib {:local/root "libs/mylib.jar"}
        
        ;; Local project (deps.edn or project.clj)
        other/project {:local/root "../other-project"}
        
        ;; Relative to user home
        user/lib {:local/root "~/.libs/mylib"}}}
```

**4. Exclusions and Overrides**
```clojure
{:deps {some/lib {:mvn/version "1.0.0"
                  :exclusions [org.clojure/clojure
                               commons-logging/commons-logging]}}
 
 ;; Force specific version (takes precedence)
 :override-deps {org.clojure/clojure {:mvn/version "1.11.1"}}}
```

**5. Optional Dependencies**
```clojure
{:aliases
 {:with-feature
  {:extra-deps {optional/feature {:mvn/version "1.0.0"}}}}}
```
How do I create custom CLI tools with tools.build?

tools.build creates uberjars, JARs, and custom build tasks:

**1. Setup build.clj**
```clojure
;; build.clj in project root
(ns build
  (:require [clojure.tools.build.api :as b]))

(def lib 'com.example/myapp)
(def version (format "1.0.%s" (b/git-count-revs nil)))
(def class-dir "target/classes")
(def basis (b/create-basis {:project "deps.edn"}))
(def uber-file (format "target/%s-%s-standalone.jar" (name lib) version))
(def jar-file (format "target/%s-%s.jar" (name lib) version))

(defn clean [_]
  (b/delete {:path "target"}))

(defn jar [_]
  (b/write-pom {:class-dir class-dir
                :lib lib
                :version version
                :basis basis
                :src-dirs ["src"]})
  (b/copy-dir {:src-dirs ["src" "resources"]
               :target-dir class-dir})
  (b/jar {:class-dir class-dir
          :jar-file jar-file}))

(defn uber [_]
  (clean nil)
  (b/copy-dir {:src-dirs ["src" "resources"]
               :target-dir class-dir})
  (b/compile-clj {:basis basis
                  :src-dirs ["src"]
                  :class-dir class-dir})
  (b/uber {:class-dir class-dir
           :uber-file uber-file
           :basis basis
           :main 'myapp.core}))

(defn install [_]
  (jar nil)
  (b/install {:basis basis
              :lib lib
              :version version
              :jar-file jar-file
              :class-dir class-dir}))
```

**2. deps.edn alias**
```clojure
{:aliases
 {:build {:deps {io.github.clojure/tools.build
                 {:git/tag "v0.9.4" :git/sha "76b78fe"}}
          :ns-default build}}}
```

**3. Run build tasks**
```bash
clj -T:build clean
clj -T:build jar
clj -T:build uber
clj -T:build install
```

**4. Custom task with params**
```clojure
(defn deploy [{:keys [repository]}]
  (jar nil)
  (println "Deploying to" repository)
  ;; Deploy logic here
  )

;; clj -T:build deploy :repository '"clojars"'
```
How do I use Clojure CLI to run scripts and one-liners?

Clojure CLI supports scripts and expressions:

**1. Run expressions (-e)**
```bash
# Simple expression
clj -e '(println "Hello")'

# Multiple expressions
clj -e '(def x 5)' -e '(println (* x x))'

# With dependencies
clj -Sdeps '{:deps {cheshire/cheshire {:mvn/version "5.12.0"}}}' \
    -e '(require (quote [cheshire.core :as json]))' \
    -e '(println (json/generate-string {:a 1}))'
```

**2. Run main function (-M)**
```bash
# Run -main in namespace
clj -M -m myapp.core

# With arguments
clj -M -m myapp.core arg1 arg2

# Using alias
clj -M:run
```

**3. Run scripts (-M with file)**
```bash
# Run Clojure file
clj -M script.clj

# Script with shebang (make executable)
#!/usr/bin/env clojure -M
(println "Hello from script!")
(println "Args:" *command-line-args*)
```

**4. Babashka for fast scripting**
```bash
# Install babashka for faster scripts
brew install borkdude/brew/babashka

# Run directly (much faster startup)
bb -e '(+ 1 2 3)'
bb script.clj

# Shebang
#!/usr/bin/env bb
(require '[babashka.fs :as fs])
(doseq [f (fs/list-dir ".")]
  (println (fs/file-name f)))
```

**5. Prep and exec (-X, -T)**
```bash
# Execute function with EDN args (-X)
clj -X:my-alias :port 8080 :host '"localhost"'

# Tool execution (-T, excludes project deps)
clj -T:build uber
```

**6. Classpath operations**
```bash
# Print classpath
clj -Spath

# Describe deps tree
clj -Stree

# Force fresh deps
clj -Sforce
```
How do I set up a REPL with nREPL and Cider middleware?

Setting up a full-featured REPL for editor integration:

**1. deps.edn configuration**
```clojure
{:paths ["src" "resources"]
 :deps {org.clojure/clojure {:mvn/version "1.11.1"}}
 
 :aliases
 {;; Basic nREPL
  :nrepl
  {:extra-deps {nrepl/nrepl {:mvn/version "1.0.0"}}
   :main-opts ["-m" "nrepl.cmdline"]}
  
  ;; nREPL with CIDER (for Emacs/Calva/etc)
  :cider
  {:extra-deps {nrepl/nrepl {:mvn/version "1.0.0"}
                cider/cider-nrepl {:mvn/version "0.40.0"}}
   :main-opts ["-m" "nrepl.cmdline"
               "--middleware" "[cider.nrepl/cider-middleware]"]}
  
  ;; With Reveal (visual REPL)
  :reveal
  {:extra-deps {vlaaad/reveal {:mvn/version "1.3.280"}}
   :jvm-opts ["-Djdk.attach.allowAttachSelf"]
   :main-opts ["-m" "nrepl.cmdline"
               "--middleware" "[cider.nrepl/cider-middleware,vlaaad.reveal.nrepl/middleware]"]}
  
  ;; With Portal (data viewer)
  :portal
  {:extra-deps {djblue/portal {:mvn/version "0.49.1"}
                nrepl/nrepl {:mvn/version "1.0.0"}}
   :main-opts ["-m" "nrepl.cmdline"]}}}
```

**2. Start REPL**
```bash
# Basic nREPL
clj -M:nrepl

# With CIDER middleware
clj -M:cider

# Specify port
clj -M:cider --port 7888

# Write port to file for editor
clj -M:cider --port 7888 --write-port-file .nrepl-port
```

**3. User-wide configuration (~/.clojure/deps.edn)**
```clojure
{:aliases
 {:nrepl {:extra-deps {nrepl/nrepl {:mvn/version "1.0.0"}
                       cider/cider-nrepl {:mvn/version "0.40.0"}}
         :main-opts ["-m" "nrepl.cmdline"
                     "--middleware" "[cider.nrepl/cider-middleware]"]}}}
```

**4. dev/user.clj for auto-loading**
```clojure
;; dev/user.clj
(ns user
  (:require [portal.api :as p]))

(defn dev-setup []
  (add-tap #'p/submit)
  (p/open))

(comment
  (dev-setup)
  (tap> {:hello "world"}))
```

Then `clj -M:dev:portal` loads both dev path and Portal.
How do I manage multiple environments and profiles in deps.edn?

Organizing deps.edn for multiple environments:

**1. Project deps.edn**
```clojure
{:paths ["src" "resources"]
 :deps {org.clojure/clojure {:mvn/version "1.11.1"}
        ;; Production deps only
        metosin/reitit {:mvn/version "0.7.0"}
        ring/ring-core {:mvn/version "1.10.0"}}
 
 :aliases
 {;; Development profile
  :dev
  {:extra-paths ["dev" "test/resources"]
   :extra-deps {ring/ring-mock {:mvn/version "0.4.0"}
                nrepl/nrepl {:mvn/version "1.0.0"}}}
  
  ;; Test profile
  :test
  {:extra-paths ["test"]
   :extra-deps {lambdaisland/kaocha {:mvn/version "1.87.1366"}}}
  
  ;; Specific test runner
  :kaocha
  {:main-opts ["-m" "kaocha.runner"]}
  
  ;; Production overrides
  :prod
  {:jvm-opts ["-Dconf=prod-config.edn"
              "-Xmx2g"
              "-server"]}
  
  ;; Local development overrides
  :local
  {:override-deps {my/lib {:local/root "../my-lib"}}}
  
  ;; AOT compilation
  :aot
  {:extra-paths ["classes"]
   :jvm-opts ["-Dclojure.compile.path=classes"]}}}
```

**2. Environment-specific configs**
```clojure
;; resources/config.edn
{:database-url #env DATABASE_URL
 :port #long #or [#env PORT 3000]}

;; Use aero for config loading
(require '[aero.core :refer [read-config]])
(def config (read-config "config.edn" {:profile :dev}))
```

**3. Combining aliases**
```bash
# Development with test
clj -M:dev:test

# Run tests in dev mode
clj -M:dev:test:kaocha

# Production run
clj -M:prod -m myapp.core

# Local lib override + dev
clj -M:dev:local
```

**4. CI-specific alias**
```clojure
{:aliases
 {:ci
  {:extra-paths ["test"]
   :extra-deps {lambdaisland/kaocha {:mvn/version "1.87.1366"}
                lambdaisland/kaocha-junit-xml {:mvn/version "1.17.101"}}
   :main-opts ["-m" "kaocha.runner"
               "--reporter" "kaocha.report/documentation"
               "--plugin" "kaocha.plugin/junit-xml"
               "--junit-xml-file" "test-results.xml"]}}}

;; In CI: clj -M:ci
```
How do I use tools.deps to resolve and download dependencies programmatically?

Using tools.deps.alpha programmatically:

```clojure
(ns build.deps
  (:require [clojure.tools.deps.alpha :as deps]
            [clojure.tools.deps.alpha.util.dir :as dir]))

;; Read deps.edn
(def deps-map (deps/slurp-deps (io/file "deps.edn")))
;; => {:paths ["src"] :deps {...} :aliases {...}}

;; Combine with user deps
(def merged-deps
  (deps/merge-edns
    [(deps/root-deps)              ; ~/.clojure/deps.edn
     deps-map]))                    ; project deps.edn

;; Create basis (resolved deps + paths)
(def basis
  (deps/create-basis
    {:project "deps.edn"
     :aliases [:dev :test]}))

;; Access resolved classpath
(:classpath-roots basis)  ; => ["src" "dev" "test" ...jars...]

;; Resolve specific deps
(def resolved
  (deps/resolve-deps
    {:deps {'org.clojure/clojure {:mvn/version "1.11.1"}
            'metosin/malli {:mvn/version "0.13.0"}}}
    nil))
;; => {org.clojure/clojure {:mvn/version "1.11.1" :paths [...]} ...}

;; Make classpath string
(deps/make-classpath-map
  {:paths ["src"]}
  resolved
  nil)
;; => {:classpath-roots [...] :classpath {...}}

;; Download specific artifact
(deps/prep-libs!
  {'some/lib {:mvn/version "1.0.0"}}
  {:action :sync
   :log :info})

;; Find all transitive deps
(defn transitive-deps [lib-map]
  (let [resolved (deps/resolve-deps {:deps lib-map} nil)]
    (into #{} (keys resolved))))

(transitive-deps {'ring/ring-core {:mvn/version "1.10.0"}})
;; => #{ring/ring-core ring/ring-codec crypto-random ...}
```

**Practical: Check for outdated deps**
```clojure
(require '[clojure.tools.deps.alpha.util.maven :as maven])

(defn latest-version [lib]
  (let [artifact (maven/coord->artifact lib {:mvn/version "RELEASE"})
        versions (maven/versions-from-repo artifact maven/central)]
    (last versions)))

(latest-version 'org.clojure/clojure)
;; => "1.11.1"
```
How do I create and use Clojure tools installed via tools.deps?

Clojure tools are globally installed utilities:

**1. Install a tool**
```bash
# Install clj-new for project generation
clj -Ttools install-latest :lib io.github.seancorfield/clj-new :as clj-new

# Install specific version
clj -Ttools install :lib io.github.seancorfield/deps-new \
                    :coord '{:git/tag "v0.5.0"}' :as new

# Install from Maven
clj -Ttools install :lib com.github.liquidz/antq \
                    :coord '{:mvn/version "2.5.1109"}' :as antq
```

**2. Use installed tools**
```bash
# List installed tools
clj -Ttools list

# Use clj-new to create project
clj -Tclj-new app :name myorg/myapp

# Use deps-new
clj -Tnew app :name myorg/myapp :target-dir myapp

# Check for outdated deps with antq
clj -Tantq outdated
```

**3. Create your own tool**
```clojure
;; my-tool/deps.edn
{:paths ["src"]
 :deps {org.clojure/clojure {:mvn/version "1.11.1"}}}

;; my-tool/src/my/tool.clj
(ns my.tool
  (:require [clojure.pprint :as pp]))

(defn greet
  "Greet someone"
  [{:keys [name greeting] :or {greeting "Hello"}}]
  (println (str greeting ", " name "!")))

(defn analyze
  "Analyze project deps"
  [{:keys [project] :or {project "deps.edn"}}]
  (let [deps (read-string (slurp project))]
    (pp/pprint {:dep-count (count (:deps deps))
                :alias-count (count (:aliases deps))})))
```

**4. Install and use your tool**
```bash
# Install from local
clj -Ttools install :lib my/tool :local/root /path/to/my-tool :as mytool

# Use it
clj -Tmytool greet :name '"World"'
clj -Tmytool analyze :project '"deps.edn"'

# Uninstall
clj -Ttools remove :tool mytool
```

**5. Common tools to install**
```bash
# deps-new - create new projects
clj -Ttools install-latest :lib io.github.seancorfield/deps-new :as new

# antq - check for outdated deps  
clj -Ttools install-latest :lib com.github.liquidz/antq :as antq

# neil - project helper
clj -Ttools install-latest :lib io.github.babashka/neil :as neil
```
